item.title: CVE-2026-133531 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.9
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.9 | A flaw was found in cluster-network-operator. The OVN IPsec certificate signer does not verify that the requested certificate Subject and DNS names belong to the requesting node. An attacker with an accepted OVN node credential and permission to submit certificate signing requests could obtain a signed certificate identifying another node. In certificate authenticated OVN IPsec deployments, this could enable peer impersonation when the attacker can also satisfy the configured peer address check, potentially compromising protected traffic.

item.title: CVE-2026-133620 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed:
- Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host. - Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository.
An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data.
Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133622 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7 | A flaw was found in certmonger. This vulnerability allows a malicious certificate authority or an attacker positioned on an unencrypted network to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending oversized or deliberately slow responses. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. Consequently, an attacker can exhaust host memory, drive CPU usage to capacity, or cause certificate requests to hang indefinitely.

item.title: CVE-2026-133626 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.
The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.
Preconditions: - An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel - Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note
Impact: - Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users - No confidentiality or integrity impact
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133627 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators).
An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records.
The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access.
Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.
